result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by an elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions between drivers and pedestrians at a marked crosswalk. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the walkway is cluttered with trash and large structural pillars that narrow the effective path.

hazards.name: Structural Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large blue steel pillars for the elevated rail structure are positioned directly at the corner, blocking the view between turning drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and middle ground along the curb line

hazards.name: Sidewalk Clutter
hazards.description: Large piles of trash bags and commercial debris significantly narrow the usable width of the sidewalk near the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk in front of the commercial storefronts

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to move pedestrians past the structural pillars before they begin their crossing, improving mutual visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals separate from vehicular traffic lights.

interventions.title: Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Improve illumination under the elevated rail structure to ensure pedestrians are visible in the shadows created by the overhead tracks.

result.summary: The intersection provides essential pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, signalized control, and paved sidewalks. However, the environment is dominated by a large elevated railway structure whose support pillars create significant visual obstructions and narrow the effective walking space at the corners.

hazards.name: Elevated Rail Pillars
hazards.description: Massive steel support pillars located at the intersection corners create significant blind spots, obscuring pedestrians from the view of turning motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left and center-right at the curb line

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk lacks any physical or vertical buffer (like trees or bollards) to protect pedestrians from traffic, particularly where the roadway narrows near the pillars.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk edges adjacent to the roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the visual obstruction of the pillars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the crosswalks to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians approaching the crossing.

interventions.title: Protective Bollards
interventions.description: Install bollards at the corners to provide physical protection for pedestrians and prevent vehicles from mounting the curb during tight turns around the pillars.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure with large support pillars that create significant visual obstructions. The intersection features wide, poorly defined asphalt areas and minimal pedestrian-specific infrastructure, leading to long crossing distances and potential conflicts with vehicles.

hazards.name: Structural Blind Spots
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated rail line obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and motorists at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right side of the image.

hazards.name: Indistinct Pedestrian Realm
hazards.description: The lack of clear vertical separation or curbing between the walking area and the roadway in the foreground creates confusion and increases risk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and bring pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the support pillars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental or ladder-style markings to clearly define pedestrian paths across the wide intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lighting underneath the elevated structure to improve visibility of pedestrians during low-light conditions.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and dedicated pedestrian signals. However, the environment is characterized by wide asphalt expanses and an overhead elevated structure that creates deep shadows, potentially impacting visibility.

hazards.name: Shadowing from Elevated Structure
hazards.description: The overhead rail structure creates significant shadows across the intersection, which can reduce the visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns across the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Enhanced Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale lighting under the elevated structure to improve visibility in shadowed areas.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.
